newsitem.title: GERMANY: Gerling open to higher Deutsche ownership.
newsitem.headline: Gerling open to higher Deutsche ownership.

text.p: German insurance group Gerling said on Thursday it wished to remain independent but would not object to its main outside shareholder Deutsche Bank AG taking a larger stake than its current 30 percent.
Gerling chairman Juergen Zech told reporters Wednesday evening that his company would take a flexible view of Deutsche Bank increasing its holding to a level below 50 percent.

At the same time, Zech said, the family-controlled insurer, a specialist in industrial cover, was capable of financing its own growth in the next seven to ten years without additional investment by Deutsche.

Gerling, fully known as Gerling Konzern Versicherungs Beteiligungs AG, also reported earnings for the business year ended June 30 1996, when its net profits slumped to 110 million marks ($69.3 million) from 274 million.

However the company stressed that its earnings from the previous period had been inflated by a one-off contribution from the sale in 1995 of its stake in reinsurance group Frankona Rueckversicherungs AG.
Its premium income for 1995/1996 rose 7.2 percent to 11.8 billion marks, amid a 12.9 percent rise in international business, compared to more modest 3.7 percent growth at home.
Although Zech said Gerling's main strategy was internal growth, he would not rule out future acquisitions.

Gerling has been setting its sights on stronger international business for several years. Foreign business accounted for 32.4 percent of Gerling's total premiums in 1995/1996, a rise from 30.6 percent.
